# Fiber Network Documentation

> Fiber Network is a peer-to-peer payment/swap network built on Nervos CKB, similar to Lightning Network. It supports multi-asset payments, cross-chain swaps with Bitcoin Lightning, and instant micropayments. This documentation covers everything from running a node to integrating Fiber into your application.

Fiber Network Node (FNN) is the reference Rust implementation. fiber-js provides a WASM node for browsers. The HTTP JSON-RPC interface allows programmatic access from any language.

## Overview

- [What is Fiber Network?](https://www.fiber.world/docs): Fiber Network is a peer-to-peer payment and swap network built on Nervos CKB. Similar to the Lightning Network, it uses 
- [How Fiber Network Works](https://www.fiber.world/docs/how-it-works): Fiber Network uses payment channels to move frequent transfers off-chain while using CKB for settlement and enforcement.

- [Overview](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/run-a-node): What it means to run a Fiber node, the available node forms, and how to pick the right deployment for your use case
- [Run a Native Node](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/run-a-node/rust): Run a native Fiber Network Node (FNN) binary on your local machine or server
- [Run a Native Node (Docker)](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/run-a-node/docker): Deploy the native Fiber Network Node using Docker
- [Run a WASM Node](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/run-a-node/fiberjs): Run a Fiber node directly in your browser app
- [Basic Transfer Example](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/basic-transfer): Learn how to set up and execute transfers between two nodes
- [Transfer Stablecoins](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/transfer-stablecoin): Learn how to transfer stablecoins between nodes
- [Multi-hop Transfers](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/multi-hop-transfer): Route Testnet payments through Fiber's public relay nodes
- [Network Resources](https://www.fiber.world/docs/quick-start/network-resources): All Fiber network resources in one place — public nodes, faucets, explorers, and more

## Build

- [Toolchain Overview](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/toolchain): A complete map of the Fiber ecosystem — tools, libraries, and how they fit together
- [JavaScript SDK](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/sdk/js): TypeScript/JavaScript SDK for Fiber Network — channels, invoices, payments, and more
- [WASM Node](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/sdk/wasm-node): Run Fiber Network node using WebAssembly
- [Overview](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/community-sdk): Community-maintained libraries and toolchains for building Fiber applications
- [fiber-pay](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/community-sdk/fiber-pay): Community toolchain for Fiber RPC, browser nodes, passkeys, React payment flows, and automation
- [fiber-checkout](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/community-sdk/fiber-checkout): Community-maintained React components and hooks for Fiber invoice checkout flows
- [Fiber FFI User Guide](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/ffi/ffi-user-guide): Embed Fiber nodes through a C ABI for mobile, desktop, and other native runtimes
- [Android Native Integration](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/ffi/android-native-integration): Integrate fiber-ffi into an Android app through JNI and the native C ABI
- [iOS Native Integration](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/ffi/ios-native-integration): Integrate fiber-ffi into an iOS app through Swift and an Objective-C bridging header
- [Using fiber-js in a Browser Extension](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/browser-extension): Guide for running @nervosnetwork/fiber-js inside a Chrome browser extension using Offscreen Documents
- [Tutorial: Build a Game](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/gaming/simple-game): A simple JavaScript game example with Fiber micro-payments
- [Game Payment Patterns](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/gaming/payment-patterns): Three ways to attach payments to a game with Fiber — pay-as-you-play, hold-invoice stakes with a trusted oracle, and adaptor-signature oracles — and how to choose between them
- [Interactive tutorials](https://www.fiber.world/docs/build/interactive-tutorials): Build and test Fiber dApps step by step in a live browser playground

## Concepts

- [Channel Lifecycle](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/channels/channel-lifecycle): Understand the ChannelState values used during a Fiber payment channel lifecycle
- [Unidirectional Channel](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/channels/unidirectional-channel): Open a one-way payment channel where funds can only flow from initiator to acceptor — ideal for streaming payments and merchant receiving
- [External Funding](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/channels/external-funding): Open a payment channel using a funding transaction signed by an external wallet
- [Channel Rebalancing](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/channels/channel-rebalancing): Shift liquidity between Fiber channels with circular payments
- [Payment Lifecycle](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/payments/payment-lifecycle): Understand how payments are created, routed, settled, and failed in the Fiber network
- [Invoice](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/payments/invoice-guide): How to create, send, parse, and manage invoices in the Fiber network
- [Hold Invoice](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/payments/hold-invoice): Deferred settlement invoices for conditional payments in the Fiber network
- [Multi-Hop Payments](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/routing/multi-hop): How Fiber routes payments through intermediate nodes using time-locked contracts and onion encryption
- [Trampoline Routing](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/routing/trampoline-routing): How Fiber delegates pathfinding to trampoline nodes so lightweight clients can route payments without a full network graph
- [Biscuit Authentication in Fiber](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/security/biscuit-auth): Overview of Biscuit authentication and how it's integrated into Fiber's RPC system
- [Watchtower](https://www.fiber.world/docs/concept/security/watchtower): How Fiber watchtower monitors channels and protects your funds from fraud

- [Module `Graph`](https://www.fiber.world/docs/api-reference/network/graph): Network graph RPC methods
- [Module `Cch`](https://www.fiber.world/docs/api-reference/cross-chain/cch): Cross Chain Hub demonstration RPC methods
- [Module `Dev`](https://www.fiber.world/docs/api-reference/dev-tooling/dev): Development-only RPC methods
- [Module `Prof`](https://www.fiber.world/docs/api-reference/dev-tooling/prof): Performance profiling RPC methods
- [Module `Watchtower`](https://www.fiber.world/docs/api-reference/dev-tooling/watchtower): Watchtower RPC methods
- [Types Reference](https://www.fiber.world/docs/api-reference/types/types): Common data types used in the JSON-RPC API
